<thought>The spectrum shows a series of peaks spaced ~1.003 Da with rapidly decreasing intensities (100 → 8 → 0.5 → 0.02 → 0.0007 → 0.00001). This is the characteristic isotopic envelope of carbon (13C ≈ 1.1 % per atom). No other element produces such a multi‑peak, 1 Da spaced pattern; chlorine, bromine, sulfur, etc., give only one or two distinct peaks. Therefore carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the observed isotopic distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
